items.q: Native or cross-platform — which is right for me?
items.a: Cross-platform (React Native / Flutter) is the right choice for most projects: one codebase ships to iOS and Android, with near-native performance and 30–50% lower development cost. We recommend native Swift or Kotlin only when the app needs heavy device-specific features (advanced AR, complex video processing, hardware integrations).

items.q: How long does it take to ship an MVP?
items.a: A typical mobile MVP ships in 8–14 weeks: 1–2 weeks discovery and design, 6–10 weeks development and QA, 1–2 weeks store submission and launch. Faster timelines are possible for narrowly scoped apps.

items.q: Do you handle App Store and Google Play submission?
items.a: Yes. We set up the developer accounts, write store descriptions, prepare screenshots and preview videos, and handle the review process — including responding to rejections. The accounts remain yours.
Every mobile project includes 1–3 months of post-launch support: bug fixes, monitoring crash reports, minor improvements, and helping with the first store update. Longer-term retainers are available.

items.q: Can you integrate with our existing backend?
items.a: Yes. We work with whatever backend you have — Spring Boot, Node.js, Django, .NET, Firebase, Supabase. If you don't have a backend yet, we build one alongside the app.

aiSearch.title: AI Search Optimization (GEO)
aiSearch.subtitle: We make your business citable by ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews, Gemini, and Claude — not just rankable on Google.

what.title: What is GEO?
what.p1: Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) is the practice of structuring a website so generative AI engines can find your content, understand it, and cite it as an answer. SEO targets the keyword ranking; GEO targets the synthesised answer itself.
what.p2: About 60% of searches now end without a click. Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT search, Perplexity, Gemini, and Claude are increasingly the first — and sometimes only — source a buyer reads. If your business is not formatted for them to quote, you are invisible in the new search layer.

why.title: Why it matters for your business

items.label: Searches end without a click — the answer is read on the results page itself.
Higher trust when AI engines cite your brand by name in a generated answer.
ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews, Gemini, and Claude all index content differently — GEO covers all of them.

geoVsSeo.title: GEO vs SEO — side by side
geoVsSeo.caption: Two different games. We play both.
rows: ChatGPT, Perplexity, AI Overviews, Gemini, Claude
Be cited inside the generated answer
Semantic clarity, structured data, brand mentions

advantage.title: EvolaTec vs a typical agency
advantage.caption: What separates a build that ranks from a build that gets quoted.
rows: FAQPage, Service, Article, BreadcrumbList — wired per page
llms.txt + clean SSR HTML + open licensing
Citation-ready Q&A passages with clear answers
Google + AI Overview + Perplexity citation tracking

checklist.title: What an EvolaTec GEO engagement delivers
checklist.caption: Every box checked on day one, not after three audits.
rows: Strict H1→H3 hierarchy, descriptive headings, accessible landmarks
llms.txt, sitemap.xml, allow-list for ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google-Extended
Self-contained answer paragraphs LLMs can quote verbatim
Named organisation and author markup for E-E-A-T
SSR + prerender, <1s LCP, AVIF/WebP images, lazy loading
Track AI Overview appearances, Perplexity citations, and brand mentions

items.a: GEO is the practice of structuring a website so generative AI engines like ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews can find your content, understand it, and cite it inside the answer they generate for a user.

items.q: How is GEO different from SEO?
items.a: SEO aims to rank your page in Google's list of blue links. GEO aims to have your content quoted inside the AI-generated answer that appears above or instead of those links. SEO is page-level; GEO is passage-level.

items.q: Do I still need SEO if I do GEO?
items.a: Yes. AI engines use search indexes as their primary source. A site that is GEO-optimised is also SEO-optimised, but the reverse is not true. We deliver both together, never one without the other.

items.q: How long until my content appears in AI answers?
items.a: Initial citations typically start within 2–6 weeks after technical GEO work ships and the AI engines recrawl the site. Brand-name mentions in ChatGPT and Perplexity often appear faster than Google AI Overview placements.

items.q: Which AI engines do you optimize for?
items.a: ChatGPT search, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews and Gemini, Claude, and Bing Copilot. We configure llms.txt and crawler allow-lists for each one and verify they can reach the content.

items.q: Can you make my existing site GEO-ready?
items.a: Yes. We run a GEO audit on the live site, add structured data, restructure key passages into citation-ready form, ship an llms.txt, and report back on which AI engines start citing the brand.

cta.title: Want a free GEO audit of your current site?
cta.subtitle: We will check structured data, AI-crawler access, citation readiness, and report back within 3 business days.
